You're right. Multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) should appear only once. I suggest keeping it under Computational Biology & Bioinformatics, where it fits alongside NMF, clustering, and statistical modeling.

Here are the revised descriptions for both sections, with clearer distinctions:

1. Transcriptomics & Multi-Omics Integration

Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, differential gene expression, pathway enrichment, immune deconvolution, molecular subtyping, and integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data.

2. Computational Biology & Bioinformatics

Development of reproducible NGS analysis workflows, statistical modeling, unsupervised clustering, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA), and interpretable machine learning.

This gives each section a distinct emphasis: Transcriptomics & Multi-Omics Integration describes the biological data and analyses, while Computational Biology & Bioinformatics highlights the computational methods and analytical frameworks.

I would retain these two revised descriptions in your website's Research Expertise section and leave the other four categories unchanged.
